nodes.label: Writing .drawio XML by hand
nodes.rationale: The geometry reference behind step 6 of the flowchart skill. Geometry hygiene matters more than it sounds, because a diagram whose arrows cross through boxes reads as careless and undermines trust in the content.

nodes.label: Child geometry is relative to the lane
nodes.rationale: The single most common source of 'why is my node outside the lane': child x/y are measured from the lane's top-left corner and the title bar is inside that box, so with startSize=40 a child at y=70 sits 30px below it. Set collapsible=0 so a reader cannot accidentally fold a lane shut, and avoid childLayout=stackLayout on the pool, which re-flows children and fights the coordinates you chose.

nodes.label: Keep every edge parented to the root
nodes.rationale: An edge parented to a lane is clipped by that lane, even when its endpoints live in different lanes. Use orthogonalEdgeStyle for right-angle routing, put the branch condition in the edge's value, and draw annotation connectors dashed with no arrowhead so they read as commentary rather than as a step.

nodes.label: Reserve a routing channel
nodes.rationale: drawio routes an unconstrained orthogonal edge through whatever is in the way, so a merge arrow will happily cut through the other branch's box. Leave an empty column inside the lane and pin the merge edge to it with exitX/entryX, or stagger the y values. Crossings between a control arrow and a data arrow are acceptable and normal; an arrow crossing through a box is not.

nodes.label: A vertical grid for row positions
nodes.rationale: Pick row positions in advance with 60-90px of clear space so labels have room. Diamonds need to be wide — 400x150 for a one-line question — because a cramped diamond wraps its text into an unreadable sliver.

nodes.label: Things that silently break
nodes.rationale: An mxGeometry without as="geometry" is ignored and the shape lands at 0,0; a source or target pointing at a missing id gives an edge floating in space with no error; two vertices sharing an id means draw.io drops one; overlapping notes just look broken. None of these raise an error, which is why the validator exists.

nodes.label: A worked critique of a failed diagram
nodes.rationale: A real diagram of what happens when an admin saves an edited employee record. It failed six ways: 76 percent one blue rectangle so shape carried no information, a process box with two unlabelled outgoing arrows where the missing question was the admin's answer, the two answers drawn as nodes instead of edge labels, two real branches (a permission gate and an absent Cancel path) hidden in sticky notes, an invisible client/server boundary that forced a box to say 'nothing is written yet' in prose, and a glossary sharing the canvas. The rebuild used three lanes, a parallelogram for the dialog, named exits including Cancel, cylinders per table, notes for explanations, and a separate glossary page.
